solved.q: Check whether the following is a valid probability distribution: X: 0, 1, 2, 3 and P(X): 0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2
steps: A probability distribution is valid if every P(X) >= 0 and the sum of all P(X) equals 1.
solved.ans: Valid probability distribution, since all probabilities are non-negative and their sum is 1

solved.topic: Finding the Constant k in a Distribution
solved.q: If X is a discrete random variable with p.m.f. P(X = x) = kx for x = 1, 2, 3, 4, find the value of k
steps: Using the property that total probability must be 1: sum of P(X=x) for all x = 1

solved.topic: Finding the Constant k in a Distribution
solved.q: If f(x) = kx for 0 <= x <= 2 and f(x) = 0 otherwise is the p.d.f. of a continuous random variable X, find k
steps: Using the property that total probability for a p.d.f. is 1: integral of f(x) dx over the whole range = 1
integral of kx dx from 0 to 2 = 1

solved.q: For the discrete random variable X with P(X=0) = 0.2, P(X=1) = 0.5, P(X=2) = 0.3, find Mean E(X) and Variance V(X)
steps: Using the formula for mean: E(X) = sum of x . P(x)
Using the formula E(X^2) = sum of x^2 . P(x)
Using the variance formula: V(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2

solved.q: For the discrete random variable X with P(X=-1) = 0.3, P(X=0) = 0.4, P(X=1) = 0.3, find Mean E(X) and Variance V(X)
steps: Using the formula for mean: E(X) = sum of x . P(x)
Using the formula E(X^2) = sum of x^2 . P(x)
Using the variance formula: V(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2

solved.q: For the discrete random variable X with P(X=1) = 0.2, P(X=2) = 0.5, P(X=3) = 0.3, find the cumulative distribution function value F(2) and hence find P(X >= 2)
steps: Using the definition of c.d.f.: F(x) = P(X <= x) = sum of all probabilities up to x
Using the complement rule: P(X >= 2) = 1 - P(X < 2) = 1 - P(X=1)

solved.q: If the p.d.f. of a continuous random variable X is f(x) = 2x for 0 <= x <= 1 and f(x) = 0 otherwise, find the c.d.f. F(x) and hence find P(0.2 <= X <= 0.5)
steps: Using the definition of c.d.f.: F(x) = integral of f(t) dt from 0 to x
F(x) = integral of 2t dt from 0 to x = [t^2] from 0 to x = x^2
Using P(a <= X <= b) = F(b) - F(a)

solved.q: Show that f(x) = (3/8)x^2 for 0 <= x <= 2 and f(x) = 0 otherwise is a valid p.d.f., and find P(X > 1)
steps: A function is a valid p.d.f. if f(x) >= 0 everywhere and the total integral over its range is 1.
Check total probability: integral of (3/8)x^2 dx from 0 to 2 = (3/8)[x^3/3] from 0 to 2
= (1/8)[x^3] from 0 to 2 = (1/8)(8 - 0) = 1, so f(x) is a valid p.d.f.
Using P(X > 1) = integral of f(x) dx from 1 to 2
solved.ans: f(x) is a valid p.d.f., and P(X > 1) = 7/8

solved.q: If the p.d.f. of a continuous random variable X is f(x) = 2x for 0 <= x <= 1 and f(x) = 0 otherwise, find E(X)
steps: Using the formula for mean of a continuous random variable: E(X) = integral of x . f(x) dx over the range
E(X) = integral of x . 2x dx from 0 to 1 = integral of 2x^2 dx from 0 to 1

solved.q: If the p.d.f. of a continuous random variable X is f(x) = 2x for 0 <= x <= 1 and f(x) = 0 otherwise, find the variance V(X)
steps: Using the formula E(X^2) = integral of x^2 . f(x) dx over the range
E(X^2) = integral of x^2 . 2x dx from 0 to 1 = integral of 2x^3 dx from 0 to 1
Using the variance formula: V(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2

solved.q: Two fair coins are tossed simultaneously. If X denotes the number of heads obtained, construct the probability distribution table of X and verify it is a valid p.m.f.
steps: Sample space when two coins are tossed: {HH, HT, TH, TT}, each with probability 1/4.
X = number of heads, so X can take values 0, 1, 2.
Check: sum of probabilities = 1/4 + 1/2 + 1/4 = 1, so it is a valid p.m.f.
solved.ans: P(X=0)=1/4, P(X=1)=1/2, P(X=2)=1/4; valid p.m.f. since sum = 1

practice.q: Check whether X: 1, 2, 3 and P(X): 0.3, 0.5, 0.4 is a valid probability distribution
practice.hint: Check that all probabilities are non-negative and that their sum equals 1.
practice.ans: Not valid, since 0.3 + 0.5 + 0.4 = 1.2, which is greater than 1
